messages:
sam: Quick follow-up to the SG pager-shim RFC — I ran a stress with RDMA fallback enabled and saw occasional ~200ms stalls on the host-staging path. Logs attached?

nina: Can you paste the exact repro? Is it when scatter-gather list grows >64 entries?

sam: Repro here (ran on dev-2):
```
# repro: stream 10k allocations with sg chains
./tools/alloc_stress --allocs 10000 --sg-threshold 48 --backend rdma
```

ben: Interesting. We saw a similar hiccup earlier but blamed NVMe driver. Did you try `--backend host` to compare?

sam: Yes — host backend steady ~8ms per batch. RDMA jumps intermittently. Stack trace shows wait on cq_poll.

prakash: Paste of tail log:
```
[2026-02-18 10:12:34] sg_build: chains=72 entries=180
[2026-02-18 10:12:34] rdma_submit: queued=1024 wait_ms=201
[2026-02-18 10:12:34] cq_poll: ret=0 timeout
```

kevin: My hunch: we don't compact SG lists before fallback, so huge scatter lists cause the kernel path to behave poorly (O(n^2) copy). Maybe add a coalesce pass on the fallback path.

nina: +1. Also think we should cap SG chain length per-tenant with a soft-fail and fall back earlier to host-copy. That avoids pathological kernel behavior.

linh: Perf numbers from my experiment: coalesce pass adds ~0.5ms but eliminates 200ms tail. Tradeoff seems worth it for p99.

infra-bot: deploy queued by @kevin for canary/rdma-fallback-coalesce v2 -> staging :rocket:

ben: Thx. Can we get a small patch that runs coalesce only when sg_len > 64 or total_bytes > 256KB?

sam: I'll draft. Also want to add a unit test that simulates many tiny fragments and asserts no >50ms stall.

prakash: Add a telemetry gauge for `sg_fallback_coalesce` so we can roll back if we see regressions. Tag metrics as `runtime/sg`.

sam: OK thanks all. I'll post PR link when ready. cc @nina @ben @kevin
